item.text:
**Bottom line:** mostly no. The best 2024 evidence is aspirational or narrow, while the operational record still points to secrecy, patronage, war extraction, and weak property/investment protections.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Weak pro | Executive Order on Russia's development goals through 2030 and for the future until 2036 | President of Russia | 2024-05-07 | https://en.special.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/73986 | Sets long-run targets for investment growth, higher living standards, fair competition, entrepreneurship, and private initiative. This is the clearest pro-competition statement, but it is an aspiration rather than proof of fair implementation. | 5B.4; also 5B.1 |
| Weak pro | Federal Law on an experimental legal regime in digital innovations | President of Russia | 2024-08-08 | https://www.kremlin.ru/acts/bank/50378/print | Creates a controlled experimental legal regime for digital innovation. That can help some entrepreneurship and investment, but the design is tightly supervised rather than broadly market-liberal. | 5B.4 |
| Against | Putin lets economically significant entities limit information disclosures | Reuters | 2024-01-29 | https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/putin-lets-economically-significant-entities-limit-information-disclosures-3315001 | Lets major firms stop disclosing some information publicly, reducing transparency and external scrutiny. That weakens investor confidence and fair commercial rules. | 5B.4; also 5B.3 |
| Against | Russia: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2024 | Says corruption is pervasive, property and business are entangled with state power, and officials and allies receive contracts and protection in return for loyalty. It also notes expropriation risk, external management of assets from “unfriendly” countries, and pressure on private firms to serve state needs. | 5B.4; also 5B.1, 5B.2 |
| Against | Russian economy shows solid growth despite Ukraine war sanctions | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-28 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/russian-economy-shows-solid-growth-despite-ukraine-war-sanctions-3591756 | Reports growth and low unemployment, but explicitly ties much of the expansion to military production. That is job creation through war mobilization, not fair rules for civilian entrepreneurship or investment. | 5B.4; also 5B.1 |
| Against | Analysis-Russia braces for more tax rises to fund the Ukraine war | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-10-31 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/analysisrussia-braces-for-more-tax-rises-to-fund-the-ukraine-war-3693480 | Says Russia would need more tax increases to finance ballooning military spending. That points to extraction for war, not stable, fair rules for private enterprise and investment. | 5B.4; also 5B.1, 5B.3 |

**Assessment**
- The strongest positive evidence is rhetorical: long-run targets plus a narrow digital-innovation pilot.
- The stronger empirical evidence points the other way: opacity for major firms, pervasive corruption, property insecurity, and war-driven economic management.
- I did not find credible 2024 evidence of a broad, predictable, pro-competition reform package that would materially improve property rights or investment conditions.

**Search gap**
- No solid 2024 evidence emerged of durable rule-of-law reforms for business, anti-corruption enforcement that constrained insiders, or broad trade/investment liberalization.
- The main “pro” material was aspirational planning language, not observable institutional change.
